decision.tag: THE DECISION YOU ARE ABOUT TO MAKE
decision.h2_a: The question is not where to move.
decision.h2_b: It is how much more the warehouse you already have can hold.
decision.sub: When a warehouse runs out of room, three options get evaluated and the fourth is usually dismissed without a look. Here are all four, with what each one costs.

options.title: Rent another warehouse
options.body: The fastest way out and the most expensive one over time, because the cost never ends and rises with every renewal. Adding 1,000 m² in premium Greater Buenos Aires runs about USD 88,000 a year, every year, without building any asset of your own.
options.note: Premium industrial rent, Greater Buenos Aires. Source: CBRE, Q2 2026.

options.title: Build a new facility
options.body: It solves the problem for a decade, but it ties up capital before a single pallet moves: you need land, permits, construction and months of running the operation alongside a building site.
options.note: Industrial facility construction cost. Source: OneMake, June 2026.

options.title: Relocate the whole operation
options.body: On top of the move itself you pay for what you do not invoice while relocating, for the time new staff take to match the old team's output and, often, for a higher rent to sit closer to demand.

options.title: Make the one you have work harder
options.cost: Up to 3 times more in the same m²
options.body: A conventional warehouse wastes air: between the aisles a forklift needs and the height nobody uses, more than half the volume stores nothing. Storing vertically and removing aisles lets the same floor area hold up to three times more, freeing up to 66% of the floor for production, docks or growth.
options.note: 3x densification versus a conventional selective racking warehouse.

decision.closing: The first three options buy new square metres. The fourth gives back the ones you are already paying for.

home.vocabPara: STOKA’s solutions span end-to-end intelligent logistics: from high-density automated warehouses to 4.0 distribution centers with industrial robotics and management software. We turn traditional warehouses and industrial buildings into automated, intelligent operations — smart warehouses, robotic warehouses and digitalized logistics plants — combining stacker cranes (the machines that rise, lower and travel between racking to store and retrieve pallets), autonomous vehicles (AGV/AMR: robots that move around the warehouse on their own, with no rails or guides) and automated storage systems to maximize space usage. If your warehouse ran out of room, if you lose time preparing orders or if rental costs keep climbing, automation stops being a luxury: it is the fastest way to organize the warehouse, gain space and cut costs without relocating or expanding.

faq.q: What is a smart warehouse?
faq.a: A smart warehouse is a facility that integrates automation, robotics and management software to operate with minimal human intervention. It combines automated storage systems (ASRS), stacker cranes, robots and real-time data to maximize density, traceability and speed. It is the evolution of the traditional warehouse toward Logistics 4.0.

faq.q: What is the difference between an automated warehouse and a traditional one?
faq.a: A traditional warehouse relies on manual work: operators walking, forklifts and static racking. An automated warehouse replaces those trips with stacker cranes, robots and software that bring the goods to the operator (goods-to-person). The result is more density per square meter, up to 99.9% accuracy, 24/7 operation and a use of vertical space impossible to achieve manually.

faq.q: Is automation worth it for SMEs?
faq.a: Yes. There are scalable automation solutions starting from USD 150,000, and in Argentina SMEs have access to tax benefits (RIMI, reduced tariff by NCM, 10.5% VAT, BICE financing) that improve the ROI. You don’t have to automate everything at once: you can start with a module — a VLM, a miniload or a picking system — and scale as the operation grows.

faq.q: How much does it cost to automate a warehouse?
faq.a: It depends on the size and the system. There are scalable solutions from USD 150,000 (a VLM or miniload module) up to full-scale projects. What matters: with the current tax benefits (RIMI, reduced tariffs) and the savings on rent and errors, the return usually falls between 18 and 36 months depending on the case. Ask for a free assessment and we’ll give you the number for YOUR case.

catalog.heroSub: Everything it takes for the warehouse you already have to hold up to three times more: AS/RS systems (automated storage and retrieval: the goods come to the operator on their own), vertical storage, robots and software, with engineering and support from Argentina.

faq.q: Can I combine systems from different categories in the same warehouse?
faq.a: Yes, it is the norm in complex projects. For example: unit-load stacker cranes for pallets in the bulk storage area + shuttle robots for high rotation + VLM for spare parts or low-rotation SKUs, all coordinated by the same WMS. System integration is part of the turnkey project.

faq.q: What is the minimum warehouse size for automation to make sense?
faq.a: There is no square-meter threshold. What determines feasibility is the volume of movements (generally more than 300–500 moves/day), the current cost of manual operation, and the available clear height. STOKA does the ROI analysis free of charge before any proposal.

faq.q: Are all catalog products available in Argentina?
faq.a: Yes. Every system in the catalog — stacker cranes, shuttle robots, VLM, conveyors and WMS/WCS software — can be installed in the country with 100% local engineering, installation and support from STOKA.

faq.q: Does the catalog include the management software or only the physical equipment?
faq.a: It includes both. The software line includes its own WMS (inventory and order management) and WCS (physical equipment control), both certified CMMI Level 5. They integrate with your existing ERP. There are also 3D visualization solutions and an HMS module (a human-machine interface to supervise the warehouse).

faq.q: Can the system be expanded in the future without stopping operations?
faq.a: Yes, all the systems we integrate are modular. A warehouse can start with 2 stacker-crane aisles and scale to 10 without stopping operations. The WMS manages the capacity expansion transparently for the existing operation.

catalog.vocabPara: The catalog covers the five building blocks of an automated warehouse: the AS/RS racking that stores at height, the robots that move the goods, the vertical towers that free up floor space, the conveyors that connect zones and the software that coordinates everything. You don't need to buy them all: each project combines only the ones the operation needs, and that combination is defined in the engineering stage, with prior flow simulation.

estanterias.label: AS/RS
estanterias.desc: Store at height and without forklift aisles: the machine goes where a person can't, so the warehouse fills up to the roof and you save the four meters of aisle that today separate each rack. It makes sense when you have free height available and many pallets of the same product. Systems available from 7 to 40 meters: drive-in, shuttle and mezzanine (AS/RS: automated storage and retrieval systems).

vertical.label: Vertical storage
vertical.desc: Store upward what takes up floor today: an enclosed tower brings the tray with the product down to the operator's height, with no walking or ladders. It makes sense when you handle many small items — spare parts, supplies, components — and floor space is at a premium. Vertical carousels and VLM units (an automated tray tower) that free up to 90% of the floor that stock occupies today (the VLM module's footprint).

robots.label: Handling robots
robots.desc: Let the goods travel to the operator instead of people walking to fetch them: fewer trips, fewer errors and a steady pace across all three shifts. They make sense when the bottleneck is order-picking speed. Stacker cranes, MiniLoad cranes (for totes and boxes instead of pallets), shuttle robots that enter the racking and AMRs (robots that move around the warehouse on their own, with no rails or guides).

transport.label: Transport equipment
transport.desc: Move loads between zones without forklifts or waiting: goods flow from one point of the warehouse to another on their own. It makes sense when there are repetitive routes between receiving, storage and dispatch. Lifts between levels, chain and roller conveyors up to 3,000 kg per pallet, and automatic palletizers.

sistema.label: Intelligent software
sistema.desc: Know where everything is so nothing depends on anyone's memory: the system records every movement and decides where to store and what to prepare first. It makes sense from day one, even before adding robots. WMS (the software that knows where everything is and decides where to store it), WCS (the one that gives the machines their movement orders), HMS (a human-machine interface to supervise the warehouse) and 3D visualization.

items.q: What is STOKA?
items.a: STOKA is an Argentine integrator of automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS), based in Maipú, Mendoza. It designs, imports, installs and maintains automated warehouses — stacker cranes, shuttle robots, vertical lift modules and WMS/WCS software — for industrial and logistics operations in Argentina and Chile.

items.q: Where is STOKA based and how far does it reach?
items.a: The base is at Carril Rodríguez Peña 35, Maipú, Mendoza. STOKA runs projects across the entire Argentine territory — Buenos Aires, Córdoba, Rosario, Mendoza and the rest of the country — and serves projects in Chile with engineering and support from Argentina, in the same time zone and the same language.

items.q: Does STOKA manufacture the equipment or import it?
items.a: It imports it and makes it run. Manufacturing is handled by specialized plants; STOKA takes care of the engineering, the sizing, the importation, the assembly, the commissioning, the integration with your management system and the support afterwards. One single point of contact, and one single party accountable for the result.

items.q: What kind of companies does STOKA work with?
items.a: With operations where the square meter is expensive or hard to come by: distribution centers, logistics operators, bonded warehouses, food and beverage plants, pharmaceutical companies, mining and cold chain. The typical size starts at warehouses of about 2,000 m² with free height available.

items.q: How is STOKA different from a global provider?
items.a: In who answers when the system stops. STOKA does the engineering, the assembly and the service with its own team in Argentina, keeps critical spare parts in the country and works in your same time zone. A provider without a local structure depends on technicians and parts that travel from abroad.

items.q: Is it better to automate the warehouse or rent another one?
items.a: It depends on how much free height you are wasting. Renting adds a permanent cost: in the premium Buenos Aires metro market, an extra 1,000 m² costs about USD 88,000 per year, every year. Automating is a one-time investment that can triple the capacity of the warehouse you are already paying for.

items.q: How much space do you recover by automating?
items.a: Up to 66% of the floor area. A conventional warehouse loses volume in two places: the aisles the forklift needs and the height nobody uses. By storing at height and eliminating aisles, the same floor area holds up to three times more goods.

items.q: When is automating NOT the right choice?
items.a: When there is no free height to take advantage of, when the warehouse has fewer than about 1,000 pallet positions, when the product mix changes completely every few months, or when the building is rented on a short lease: the investment stays tied to a property that isn't yours.

items.q: How much free height do I need?
items.a: From 7 meters up there are already systems that perform, although the big jump appears from 10 to 12 meters. Systems go up to 40 meters. With less than 7 meters, it is worth looking at vertical tower storage before a full pallet system.

items.q: Does it work for a small warehouse?
items.a: Yes, but with a different technology. In small floor areas, vertical lift modules and tote systems perform better than a full pallet ASRS: they take up a few square meters of floor, reach 10 meters in height and bring the goods to the operator with no structural construction work.

items.q: How much does it cost to automate a warehouse in Argentina?
items.a: It depends on the number of positions and the required speed, not on the square meters. A typical project of 1,000 to 3,000 positions sits in the range of hundreds of thousands of dollars. The price is defined after the site survey, not before: the only serious way to give a number is to measure the operation.

items.q: How long does it take to recover the investment?
items.a: Between 18 and 36 months in most projects. The timeframe depends above all on the cost of the square meter in your area: the more expensive the rent you stop paying, the faster the investment comes back. In areas with cheap rent, the return stretches out.

items.q: Can it be financed?
items.a: Yes. There are bank credit lines for capital goods and leasing, with terms of up to 10 years. Rates and terms change often, so they are quoted at the time of the operation. STOKA prepares the technical file the bank asks for.

items.q: Are there tax benefits for this type of investment?
items.a: Yes, and they have to be analyzed case by case. There are promotion regimes for capital goods with accelerated depreciation and VAT recovery, subject to requirements such as the MiPyME certificate and minimum amounts. STOKA provides the technical documentation; the tax treatment is defined by your accountant.

items.q: What costs does the system have after you buy it?
items.a: Preventive maintenance, wear parts and energy. Scheduled maintenance takes a few hours per month and is planned outside peak hours. The total cost over ten years is usually lower than that of an equivalent European system, above all because of response times and technician travel.

items.q: What is an ASRS system?
items.a: An ASRS is an automated storage and retrieval system: machines that store and retrieve goods without a person entering the storage area. Instead of the operator going to fetch the product, the system brings it to them. That makes it possible to store at height and without aisles.

items.q: What is the difference between a stacker crane and a shuttle robot?
items.a: The stacker crane is a machine that travels along a fixed aisle, rising and lowering to store and retrieve pallets. The shuttle robot goes inside the racking and moves along the channels. The stacker crane performs better at height; the shuttle, in density and in movements per hour.

items.q: What is a WMS and how is it different from a WCS?
items.a: The WMS is the software that knows where everything is and decides where to store it; the WCS is the one that gives the machines their movement orders. The WMS thinks, the WCS executes. An automated system needs both, and they usually come integrated.

items.q: Does it integrate with my ERP?
items.a: Yes. Integration is done through a data interface and is already solved for the systems most used in Argentina and Chile: SAP, Oracle, Tango and in-house developments. It is defined in the engineering stage, not at the end: what information travels, at what moment and in which direction.

items.q: Does it work in a cold room?
items.a: Yes. There is equipment prepared for positive and negative cold: stacker cranes operate down to -30 °C and shuttle robots down to -25 °C. Besides solving the operation, they take staff out of the chamber, which is where the cold hits hardest in absenteeism and labor cost.

items.q: What happens if the power goes out?
items.a: The system stops safely and holds the position of every load. When power returns, the software rebuilds the inventory state and resumes from where it left off, with no loss of traceability. For critical operations, backup power is sized in the engineering stage.

items.q: How much maintenance does it need?
items.a: Scheduled preventive maintenance, on the order of a few hours per month, plus replacement of the highest-wear components according to hours of use. It is planned in windows outside the operating peak. STOKA keeps critical spare parts in Argentina so a failure doesn't stop the operation for weeks.

items.q: Do we have to stop the operation during installation?
items.a: Not entirely. Assembly is planned by sectors so the warehouse keeps operating, and migration is done in stages. Stoppage windows are agreed in the schedule before starting, and they usually concentrate on the commissioning and on the migration of the inventory.

items.q: Who trains the staff?
items.a: STOKA does, on site and with the system already installed. Training covers daily operation, resolving the most frequent incidents and using the management software. The typical learning curve is days, not months: the operator stops searching for goods and moves to working at a fixed station.

items.q: Does automating mean laying people off?
items.a: Not necessarily. In most projects, staff are reassigned to higher-value tasks — quality control, preparing special orders, supervising the system — and what gets eliminated is the walking, the pallet hauling and the picking errors. The decision about headcount belongs to each company.

items.q: What about support and spare parts after the sale?
items.a: The same team that did the project handles them. STOKA keeps an inventory of critical spare parts in Argentina and provides technical support in Spanish, in your same time zone. Only what requires factory intervention escalates abroad; the rest is resolved in the country.

items.q: Does STOKA work in Chile?
items.a: Yes. Chilean projects are served with engineering and support from Argentina: same time zone, same language and coordinated technical site visits. The team can visit your facilities, diagnose the operation and present a turnkey proposal under the same conditions as in Argentina.

faq.q: How long does it take to implement an ASRS system?
faq.a: It depends on scale. A medium system (5,000–20,000 positions) generally takes 6–12 months from contract signing to startup. Larger projects may require 12 to 18 months.

faq.q: Do I need to change my ERP to implement an automated system?
faq.a: No. Our systems integrate with the main ERPs on the market (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, etc.) through standard APIs. Integration is part of the project scope.

faq.q: What happens if there's a power outage or technical failure?
faq.a: The systems we integrate have emergency operation protocols, UPS, and optional generators. The WMS preserves inventory state and equipment automatically resumes from where they were.

faq.q: Can you finance the project in Argentina?

faq.q: What is Logistics 4.0?
faq.a: Logistics 4.0 is the application of Industry 4.0 technologies —automation, IoT, artificial intelligence and data analytics— to warehouse operations and the supply chain. It lets warehouses, stacker cranes, robots and software communicate with each other for a connected, autonomous and self-optimizing operation. In practice, it turns a traditional warehouse into a smart warehouse.

faq.q: How much space does an ASRS system save?
faq.a: An ASRS system uses the height of the building —from 7 up to 40 meters— and eliminates the wide aisles forklifts require. In practice, a high-density automated warehouse can store up to 3 times more goods in the same square meter than conventional racking — and up to 5 times with 12 meters of height or more and a homogeneous product — freeing up space or avoiding a building expansion.

faq.q: What is intralogistics?
faq.a: Intralogistics is the set of material and information flow processes inside a warehouse or plant: receiving, storage, order picking and dispatch. Automated intralogistics —with stacker cranes, robots and management software— is the heart of smart logistics and the Warehouse 4.0.

The online channel in Argentina and Chile grew more than 40% per year between 2020 and 2024. That growth is not just opportunity: it is pressure on automated fulfillment centers and distribution centers that must dispatch orders ever faster and at an ever lower cost per unit. Automated ecommerce order picking —the most labor-intensive process of e-commerce— benefits most from fulfillment automation: an ASRS system with shuttle robots and MiniLoad stacker cranes multiplies throughput without multiplying headcount.

The systems we implement for e-commerce include automatic returns management —one of the channel's biggest pains—, dynamic slotting that optimizes SKU location based on real-time sales history, and a WMS interface that integrates directly with the e-commerce platforms most used in the region. For companies running a micro fulfillment center or an automated dark store, these systems offer the density and speed those formats demand. The result: the fulfillment center processes the same volume with fewer staff, fewer errors and faster dispatch. During seasonal peaks like Hot Sale or Black Friday, the system scales without hiring extra staff.

faq.q: How long does it take to implement an ASRS system for e-commerce?
faq.a: An e-commerce fulfillment automation project takes between 4 and 8 months from the initial consultation to operational start-up. The engineering phase runs in parallel with equipment manufacturing, which compresses timelines. STOKA manages the turnkey project from design to staff training.

faq.q: How does the fulfillment center handle demand peaks like Black Friday?
faq.a: The ASRS does not require hiring extra staff to absorb peaks. Throughput increases by activating more robots or picking stations. An automated fulfillment center can handle 5x the usual volume with no infrastructure changes, something impossible with manual operation in the same timeframe.

faq.q: What real order picking speed can I expect?
faq.a: Depending on the SKU profile, the systems we integrate reach between 800 and 1,200 lines per hour per station in goods-to-person picking. The improvement across the full order-preparation process is on the order of 3x; the per-station jump is larger when the baseline is manual picking with long walking routes (150-200 lines per hour).

faq.q: Does the WMS integrate with my ERP or e-commerce platform?
faq.a: Yes. The WMS has native connectors for SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics and RESTful APIs for any system. Integration with platforms like Shopify, VTEX or Magento is possible through standard middleware.

3PL logistics operators in Argentina and Chile face constant pressure: clients demand more services, more visibility and lower costs while margins compress. A logistics operator's real competitive differentiation in this context comes from logistics operator automation: warehouse automation 3PL —real-time inventory visibility, per-client reports and 24/7 operation— has a value proposition the rest cannot match with manual infrastructure.

Automating the multi-client warehouse also enables value-added services that were previously inaccessible: high-speed unit picking, e-commerce returns management, temperature picking for fresh or pharmaceutical products, and cross docking automation for high-rotation flows with no intermediate storage. The multi-client WMS we implement lets one multi-client warehouse simultaneously serve clients with very different operating profiles —mass consumption, pharma, textile— with fully segregated inventories and no mixing. This flexibility turns the logistics operator into a strategic partner of the client, not just a space provider.

faq.q: Can I manage multiple clients in the same automated multi-client warehouse?
faq.a: Yes. The WMS supports multi-client logical and physical segregation in the same multi-client warehouse. Each client has its own inventory, reports and separate KPIs without physically separating the zones.

faq.q: What happens if I lose a client or the contract changes?
faq.a: Slots are dynamic: you can reassign space between clients without physically moving the goods. If a client reduces volume, that space becomes available automatically.

faq.q: How do I bill space and movements to each client?
faq.a: The WMS generates detailed per-client reports: occupied positions, inbound, outbound and processed orders. This data is exported in standard formats for billing.

faq.q: How much does automation reduce the operating cost of a 3PL logistics operator?
faq.a: In typical 3PL operations, automation reduces labor cost by 40% to 55%. The system operates 24/7 with no productivity variation or extra cost in high season.

In the manufacturing industry of Argentina and Chile, plant logistics —the plant's internal logistics— is the bottleneck that most affects productive efficiency. The automated raw-material warehouse and automated line feeding eliminate stoppages: a production line that stops for lack of inputs loses between USD 500 and USD 5,000 per hour. The production buffer synchronized with the MES, the basis of automated just in time, eliminates that risk.

The automated finished-goods warehouse solves the other end: agile and accurate dispatch of orders to the distribution channel. With plant logistics synchronized with the ERP via WCS, load preparation starts automatically without human intervention. Lot and serial number traceability is recorded in every depot movement, speeding up audits and market recalls.

faq.q: Can I integrate plant logistics directly with my production line?
faq.a: Yes. The systems we integrate connect with the plant MES (Manufacturing Execution System). When the line needs an input, the MES automatically sends the order to the depot WCS, enabling automated just in time.

faq.q: What happens if there is a power outage during operation?
faq.a: The systems we implement have integrated UPS and automatic recovery protocols. In case of an outage, the system records the exact position of each robot and recovers from the interruption point with no data loss.

faq.q: Can I implement the system in phases without stopping production?
faq.a: Yes. Phased implementation is the usual strategy: first the raw-material or finished-goods warehouse, without touching the production line.

faq.q: What level of maintenance does the in-plant system require?
faq.a: Preventive maintenance equals 2-4 hours per month for a standard system. The WCS monitors each component and issues early alerts before a failure occurs.

alimentos-bebidas.seo:
Food logistics in Argentina and Chile operates under permanent tension between storage cost and safety requirements. Large chains demand complete food traceability, guaranteed expiry dates and identification errors that drop to nearly zero (99.9% accuracy). The automated food warehouse and the automated cold storage warehouse for beverages are the most reliable way to guarantee that consistently at industrial scale.

The ASRS systems we implement for food logistics include a native FEFO (First Expired, First Out) module in the WMS, a complement to automatic FIFO: at every dispatch, the system automatically selects the product with the nearest expiry without relying on the operator's judgment. This cuts expiry waste to a minimum, reduces recall risk and guarantees compliance with the food traceability requirements of large buyers.

faq.q: Does the system guarantee automatic FIFO in food logistics?
faq.a: Yes, automatic FIFO is native. The WMS records the production and expiry date of each lot at receipt. At every dispatch, the system automatically selects the product with the oldest receipt date without relying on the operator.

faq.q: At what temperatures do robots operate in the cold storage warehouse?
faq.a: The stacker cranes and shuttle robots operate between -5°C and +10°C in refrigerated format; in frozen format, the shuttle robots reach -25 °C and the stacker cranes -30 °C in the cold storage warehouse. They feature anti-condensation hermetic sealing and special cold lubrication.

faq.q: How does the system speed up a market recall?
faq.a: With complete food traceability, a recall that normally takes days is executed in minutes. The WMS locates all depots holding goods from the affected lot and automatically blocks dispatches of the compromised stock.

faq.q: What quality certifications does the system have for food logistics?
faq.a: These systems are compatible with GS1, FSSC 22000 and BRC. The WMS generates records in an auditor-ready format that meet the requirements of these certifications.

farmaceutica.seo:
The pharmaceutical warehouse is the most regulated environment in pharmaceutical logistics. National (ANMAT in Argentina) and international (FDA, EMA, WHO GDP) regulations require complete medicine traceability of each unit from receipt to dispatch, temperature and humidity control with continuous records, and role-based controlled access with an immutable audit trail in the GMP warehouse.

The GMP-compliant WMS we implement meets 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11 and ANMAT requirements. For laboratories, drug wholesalers and pharmaceutical distributors in Argentina and Chile, automating the pharma depot with STOKA includes pre-built IQ/OQ/PQ documentation that significantly reduces the time and cost of the regulatory qualification process.

faq.q: Does the system comply with GMP and ANMAT regulations for the GMP warehouse?
faq.a: Yes. The WMS includes a GMP module that records every movement with user, timestamp, origin and destination location. This audit trail complies with 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11 and ANMAT requirements.

faq.q: How does role-based access control work in the pharma depot?
faq.a: Each operator has unique credentials with permissions by zone, operation type and product. The system records who did what and when in every movement, guaranteeing medicine traceability.

faq.q: Can differentiated temperature zones be created in the same depot?
faq.a: Yes. The system allows defining logical zones with specific temperature requirements (2-8°C, 15-25°C, -20°C) within the same GMP warehouse. Temperature monitoring is continuous with automatic alerts on deviations.

faq.q: How long does it take to validate the system for GMP in a pharma depot?
faq.a: IQ/OQ/PQ validation takes between 3 and 6 months post-installation. The manufacturer delivers validation documentation (DQ, FS, DS) with the system.

faq.q: Does the system manage the unit serialization required by ANMAT?
faq.a: Yes. The WMS serialization module reads and records the barcode or 2D DataMatrix of each unit in receiving, storage and dispatch operations, ensuring medicine traceability.

faq.q: Can the system be used in a wholesaler with GDP authorization?
faq.a: Yes. The WMS we implement has been qualified in facilities with GDP authorization in Latin America.

faq.q: How are expired or recalled medicines handled?
faq.a: The WMS has a specific quarantine and destruction flow: blocked products are logically segregated, with automatic dispatch blocking and notification to the regulatory officer.

faq.q: How much vertical space does an AS/RS system use in my warehouse or facility?
faq.a: The AS/RS systems we integrate use from 7 to 40 meters of free height. In a warehouse with 12 meters of height you can store up to 3 times more than with conventional 4-5 meter racking; with a homogeneous product and greater heights, the ratio can reach 5 times. faq.q: What is the difference between drive-in, shuttle and MiniLoad racking?
faq.a: Drive-in racking uses conventional forklifts: the most economical, ideal for high-density LIFO. Shuttle racking combines racking with shuttle robots for higher speed and selective FIFO/LIFO. MiniLoad is for containers and totes with stacker cranes: maximum speed and precision for e-commerce, pharma and high-rotation facilities.

faq.q: How long does it take to install an AS/RS system in an existing warehouse?
faq.a: The mechanical installation of AS/RS racking takes 4 to 10 weeks depending on the model. Prior civil works (flat slab, lighting) can add 4-6 weeks if the building requires it. STOKA coordinates all detailed engineering, assembly and certified commissioning in Argentina.

faq.q: Does the racking qualify for the reduced tariff under Decreto 513/2025 in Argentina?
faq.a: They may apply. Decree 513/2025 covers 27 capital-goods tariff positions and reduces the import tariff according to the NCM classification of each component; you need to check whether your project's equipment is on the list. STOKA verifies the tariff position with your customs broker before importation, at no additional cost.

faq.q: What is a smart warehouse and how does it differ from a traditional one?
faq.a: A smart warehouse is an automated warehouse that integrates ASRS systems, robotics and management software to operate with minimal human intervention. Unlike a traditional warehouse —with operators, forklifts and static racking—, the smart warehouse brings goods to the operator (goods-to-person), multiplies density per square meter and operates 24/7 with full traceability. It is the basis of Logistics 4.0 and modern intralogistics.

faq.q: How much space does an ASRS system save in a distribution center?
faq.a: An ASRS system uses the height of the building —from 7 to 40 meters— and eliminates the wide forklift aisles. In practice, a high-density robotized warehouse can store up to 3 times more goods in the same square meter than conventional racking — and up to 5 times with 12 meters of height or more and a homogeneous product — freeing up floor space or avoiding a building expansion of the distribution center.

faq.q: What is the difference between a stacker crane and a shuttle robot in a warehouse?

faq.q: When is a VLM better and when is a vertical carousel better for my warehouse?
faq.a: The VLM is best when you have high SKU variety and need random access: each cycle you can retrieve any tray independently. The carousel is more efficient for high-turnover SKUs with sequential access. For pharma, spare parts and e-commerce with many different SKUs, the VLM is generally the best option.

faq.q: How much floor space do I save with a VLM in my warehouse?
faq.a: Typically between 70% and 90% of the floor footprint compared with conventional shelving. A 10-meter-high VLM occupies a footprint of about 9 m² (3×3 m) and stores the equivalent of 30–50 m² of conventional shelving: those floor square meters are freed up for production, picking or growth.

faq.q: How does the VLM integrate with my existing ERP or WMS?

If you already have a third-party WMS (SAP EWM, Manhattan, etc.), the VLM can operate as a slave subsystem that receives extraction orders. If you don't have a WMS, the built-in management module manages warehouse inventory autonomously with ERP integration.

faq.q: Can the VLM or vertical carousel operate in temperature-controlled environments?
faq.a: The vertical carousel operates between -5°C and +40°C, compatible with positive cold rooms. The VLM has versions for environments between 2°C and 25°C, ideal for pharma and refrigerated products. For negative cold (frozen storage), the specialized AS/RS-line stacker cranes are recommended.

beneficiosFiscales.rimiCalificaP: It depends on the NCM position of each piece of equipment, not on the system as a whole. New movable goods classified as Capital Goods (BK) or IT and Telecommunications Goods (BIT) under Annex I of Decreto 557/2023 qualify. beneficiosFiscales.rimiB1H3: Benefit 1 — Accelerated depreciation for Income Tax
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB1P: Instead of depreciating the asset over its useful life, RIMI allows you to deduct 100% of the acquisition value in two equal annual installments. Important: accelerated depreciation does not reduce the total tax, it brings the deduction forward. You deduct more at the start and less later, so over the asset's life you pay the same — but you pay later, and that money keeps working in your company. The benefit is financial, a cash-flow benefit.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB1Ej1: Investment in an ASRS system: USD 2,000,000.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB1Ej2: USD 1,000,000 is deducted in the first fiscal year. At a 35% rate, that is roughly USD 350,000 less Income Tax that year.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB1Ej3: a deduction of USD 200,000/year → roughly USD 70,000 less Income Tax over the same period. The USD 280,000 difference is not new money: it is the same tax, paid later.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB2P: The VAT paid on the import or the local purchase is a tax credit: it is offset against the VAT your company charges on its sales. When that credit is not absorbed, the general regime only lets you request a refund after six tax periods. RIMI shortens that wait to three. The benefit is subject to an annual quota: the RIMI refund cannot exceed 50% of the regime's quota and is allocated by the age of the accumulated balances.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB2Ej1: Import of an ASRS system for USD 2,000,000.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB2Ej2: The VAT on the operation is calculated on the CIF value. Most machinery is taxed at 10.5%; structural racking and parts, at 21%. On a USD 2,000,000 project with 70% covered machinery, that is on the order of USD 273,000 of tax credit to recover.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiB2Ej3: Without the regime, that credit is absorbed gradually against the VAT on your sales, tying up working capital in the meantime.
beneficiosFiscales.rimiLimitH3: RIMI limitations to keep in mind

rimiLimits.title: Budget quota
rimiLimits.desc: The quota applies to the VAT benefit, not to accelerated depreciation. The RIMI refund is capped at 50% of the regime's annual quota and is allocated by the age of the accumulated balances. There is no public information on the status of the 2026 quota.

rimiLimits.title: Investment Management System (SGI)
rimiLimits.desc: Registration is done through the SGI of ARCA (Argentina's tax agency). When RG 5849/2026 was published, the platform was not yet operational. Check its availability before planning the project schedule.

rimiLimits.title: Asset retention
rimiLimits.desc: The asset must remain in the company's equity for 2 fiscal years. If it leaves earlier, the benefit lapses and must be repaid with interest.

rimiLimits.title: The election is all-or-nothing
rimiLimits.desc: If you opt for accelerated depreciation, it applies to all your RIMI investments in the period: you cannot choose asset by asset. RIMI is also incompatible with RIGI on the same investments.

beneficiosFiscales.ivaBienesUsoP: This is the regime that applies when the investment does not reach the RIMI minimum, and it has no amount floor. It allows you to request a refund of the VAT credit originated in fixed assets that has not been absorbed after six consecutive tax periods. It is processed through the SIR system, once per calendar year, with a report from an independent certified public accountant.
beneficiosFiscales.ivaBienesUsoNota: The pre-application is filed between December 1 and 15. It is subject to an annual quota. Regulations: unnumbered article following art. 24 of Ley 23.349 · RG AFIP 5298/2022.
beneficiosFiscales.ivaBienesUsoDest: If your company is Small and the investment is between USD 200,000 and USD 600,000, this is the regime that applies to you: RIMI requires a minimum of USD 600,000 for your category.
beneficiosFiscales.rigiH2: RIGI — If your project exceeds USD 200 million

A typical ASRS system (USD 500K–5M) does not reach that threshold on its own — but if your company already has a project admitted to RIGI, the warehouse automation component can enter as part of the approved promoted investment.

beneficiosFiscales.rigiKeyP: If your company has a project admitted to RIGI, your ASRS system fits within the promoted investment package. We help you structure the technical documentation of the automation component so it is properly included in the approved filing.
beneficiosFiscales.rigiLegal: Regulations: Ley 27.742 · Decreto 749/2024. Joining RIGI is voluntary and involves minimum investment commitments. Verify eligibility with a specialized legal advisor.
beneficiosFiscales.arancelH2: Reduced import duties for capital goods
beneficiosFiscales.arancelIntro: The import duty on an automated storage system is not a single rate: it depends on the NCM position of each component and ranges from 0% to 12.6%. Decreto 513/2025, which replaced the Capital Goods annex of Decreto 557/2023, brings 379 tariff positions down to 2%, among them industrial robots and electric stackers. It does not set a 0% duty for any position.
beneficiosFiscales.arancelKeyTag: The fact that changes the project's numbers
beneficiosFiscales.arancelKeyP: The stacker crane — the biggest-ticket item in a pallet ASRS — pays 0% import duty under the Common External Tariff, not under a promotional regime. Conveyors and structural racking, by contrast, pay considerably more. That is why a project's average duty depends on its composition, and the classification of each component is determined by the customs broker, not the supplier. STOKA provides the technical data sheets that classification requires.
beneficiosFiscales.arancelWarn: New capital goods are exempt from the 3% statistics fee (Decreto 690/02, art. 26 inc. g). If they are also recorded as fixed assets, no VAT or Income Tax advance collections apply. The PAIS tax is no longer in force: it expired in December 2024.
beneficiosFiscales.arancelLegal: Regulations: Decreto 557/2023, Anexo I · Decreto 513/2025 (replaces the Capital Goods annex) · Decreto 690/2002 art. 26 · Decreto 1140/2024 (statistics fee). Verify the NCM position of each component with a licensed customs broker.
beneficiosFiscales.ivaH2: VAT reduced to 10.5% for capital goods
beneficiosFiscales.ivaIntro: Article 28, subsection e) of the VAT law (Ley 23.349, consolidated text per Decreto 280/97) sets a 10.5% rate — half the general rate — for the goods included in its Annexed Schedule, both on local sale and on definitive import. The machinery of an automated system is covered: stacker cranes, conveyors, stackers and machines with an individual function. Metal racking and spare parts are not on that schedule and pay 21%.
beneficiosFiscales.ivaImpactTag: Impact on a USD 2,000,000 project (if the equipment's NCM qualifies for 10.5%)
beneficiosFiscales.ivaNota: For a registered VAT taxpayer, the VAT on the import is not money lost: it is a tax credit offset against the VAT your company charges on its sales. The difference between 21% and 10.5% is not less tax: it is less capital tied up and less time until you recover it.
beneficiosFiscales.ivaWarn: If the operation is structured via leasing, the VAT accrues with each lease payment rather than in a single upfront disbursement. The treatment of the rate applicable to the lease payments is determined by your tax advisor based on how the contract is framed.

beneficiosFiscales.ctx2026H2: Why 2026 is a window of opportunity to automate
ctx2026P: The convergence of three factors makes 2025–2026 a unique window to invest in warehouse automation in Argentina. For the first time in decades, long-term regulatory stability, lower import duties and access to preferential financing come together at the same time.

RIMI lets MiPyMEs deduct the asset in two equal annual installments and shortens the VAT recovery on the investment from six to three periods; and when the amount does not reach the regime's minimum, the VAT refund on fixed assets (RG 5298/2022) has no floor. That shorter recovery horizon makes it easier to calculate TCO (what the system costs over its whole life, not just to buy it) and to present the project to the board or to lenders.

The capital goods annex of Decreto 557/2023, as amended by Decreto 513/2025, brings 379 tariff positions down to 2%. On the CIF value of the imported equipment of a USD 800,000 project, the duty savings versus the general rate are in the range of USD 20,000 to 50,000 depending on the system's composition.

The combination of BICE + RIMI + reduced import duty transforms the investment equation: the monthly financing installment is compared directly against the labor cost being replaced and, in many projects, the system pays for itself with the savings it generates from the first year of operation.

faqItems.q: Does an imported ASRS system qualify as a capital good for RIMI?
faqItems.a: It depends on the NCM position of each component. New movable goods classified as Capital Goods (BK) or IT and Telecommunications Goods (BIT) under Annex I of Decreto 557/2023 qualify: stacker cranes, shuttles and conveyors classify as BK; control hardware, as BIT. Software (WMS/WCS) is an intangible: it does not enter the regime as a depreciable asset.

faqItems.q: How much can I really save?
faqItems.a: It depends on the amount, your MiPyME category and the system's composition. What actually reduces the cost is the import duty and the differential VAT: between 8% and 15% of the imported equipment's value. Accelerated depreciation and VAT recovery do not lower the total tax; they improve cash flow.

faqItems.q: Does STOKA handle the tax filings?
faqItems.a: No. STOKA supports you with the equipment's technical documentation (data sheets, NCM positions, capital-good classification). RIMI/RIGI adhesion and the tax filings are handled by your accountant or tax advisor.

It requires case-by-case analysis with your tax advisor. RIMI requires the asset to remain in the company's equity for 2 fiscal years, and in a lease legal ownership stays with the lessor until the purchase option is exercised. It is a compatibility issue to resolve before signing, not after.

faqItems.q: What if my company is not an SME?
faqItems.a: If you are not an SME and your project does not reach USD 200M (RIGI), you can still take advantage of: reduced import duties, 10.5% VAT (if the NCM qualifies), leasing and provincial benefits depending on your location.

faqItems.q: Do RIGI benefits apply to the ASRS within a mining or oil project?
faqItems.a: Only if your company already has a project admitted to RIGI: an ASRS does not access the regime on its own; it enters as part of the approved project's promoted investment. In that case, the project's capital goods enjoy full exemption from import duties and VAT via tax credit certificates.

faqItems.q: How much does it cost to automate a warehouse?
faqItems.a: It depends on the technology, the required throughput (the movements per hour the system must handle) and the size of the warehouse. As a reference: a VLM module or a picking system can start from USD 150,000; a compact shuttle system runs around USD 600,000; and a complete unit-load ASRS with software can exceed USD 3,000,000. In Argentina, the import duty and the differential VAT reduce the effective cost by between 8% and 15% of the imported equipment's value; RIMI, the VAT refund and financing also improve cash flow, but they are deferral, not a discount.

faqItems.q: Should I automate my warehouse now or wait?
faqItems.a: The combination of benefits in force in 2026 makes this moment a favorable window: RIMI brings the asset's deduction forward and shortens VAT recovery, Decreto 513/2025 reduces import duties based on NCM classification, and the BICE line finances up to 80% of the project over 10 years. This convergence of incentives, duty reduction and preferential financing is not always available at the same time.

faqItems.q: My company is Small and the investment is USD 300,000. Do I qualify for RIMI?
faqItems.a: No. For the Small category the RIMI minimum is USD 600,000, computed by adding up eligible investments within a 2-year window. With USD 300,000, the instrument that applies to you is the general regime of VAT refund on fixed assets, which has no minimum amount.

faqItems.q: Does accelerated depreciation make me pay less tax?
faqItems.a: No: it makes you pay it later. You deduct more at the start and less afterwards, so over the asset's life the total tax is the same. The benefit is financial: that money keeps working in your company instead of sitting prepaid with the tax authority.
